entities.summary:
The Prime Minister of Afghanistan was a high-ranking political office in the country, playing a crucial role in shaping the nation's politics and governance from the 20th century onwards. 

The office was first established in the early 20th century, following the country's independence from British colonial rule. The Prime Minister was responsible for advising the monarch and overseeing the administration of the government. 

One of the most notable Prime Ministers of Afghanistan was Mohammad Daoud Khan, who served from 1953 to 1963 and implemented various modernization policies, including the establishment of a national police force and the development of the country's infrastructure. 

The Prime Minister of Afghanistan continued to play a significant role in the country's politics until the 1978 Saur Revolution, which led to the establishment of a communist government and the eventual collapse of the monarchy. 

The legacy of the Prime Minister's office continues to be felt in Afghanistan today, with many politicians and leaders drawing on the experience and wisdom of those who held the office in the past.
